classification.difficultyReason: Track which individual socks remain without replacement, retain separate paths for the two red socks, and combine both selection orders for colour events before counting favourable paths out of twelve; the supplied branches scaffold these linked procedures.

inlines.text: A drawer contains two red socks (R), one blue sock (B) and one yellow sock (Y).
Two socks are selected at random

spec.description: First-stage branch strokes. The adjacent native label table supplies R, R, B and the Y cloze. Together with the second-stage branch strokes and terminal table, these form one editable tree.
spec.mathematics: Four distinguishable first selections; the two red socks retain separate branches.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source-supplied labels are permanent; missing labels are native clozes.

spec.description: Each first-stage branch splits into three remaining individual-sock selections. Native terminal rows align with the twelve branch endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Three socks remain after every first selection, giving twelve equally likely ordered individual selections.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers are embedded in the branch strokes.

answer.short: First sock: R, R, B, Y. Second socks and outcomes, by branch: R → R, B, Y: RR, RB, RY; R → R, B, Y: RR, RB, RY; B → R, R, Y: BR, BR, BY; Y → R, R, B: YR, YR, YB.
answer.worked: Keep a separate branch for each red sock. After the first sock is selected, three individual socks remain. The twelve paths are RR, RB, RY, RR, RB, RY, BR, BR, BY, YR, YR, YB. Repeated colour outcomes represent different individual-sock selections.

spec.description: Complete two-stage tree with four first-stage branches and twelve terminal paths; both red socks remain separate.
spec.mathematics: Ordered selections without replacement: RR, RB, RY; RR, RB, RY; BR, BR, BY; YR, YR, YB.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution figure shown in answer editions.

children.label: i
children.prompt: a red sock and a blue sock

answer.worked:
There are four favourable paths: two RB and two BR.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{red and blue})&=\frac{4}{12}\\&=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$$

Two of the twelve paths are RR.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{two red})&=\frac{2}{12}\\&=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: any pair of socks of the same colour

answer.worked:
Only the two RR paths have matching colours; there is only one blue sock and one yellow sock.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{2}{12}\\&=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: iv
children.prompt: any pair of socks of different colour

answer.worked:
Ten of the twelve paths have different colours.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{different colours})&=\frac{10}{12}\\&=\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}$$
